\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صحو} (ṣaḥw)}{صحو (ṣaḥw)}]{\ar{صحو} (ṣaḥw) — clear weather; cloudless}

\label{lesson:AR-C485-sahw}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for drought, then the Arabic for to evaporate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صحو}}
\textbf{\ar{صحو}} — \emph{ṣaḥw} — \textquotedblleft{}clear weather; cloudless\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{الطقس} \ar{صحو} \ar{اليوم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aṭ-ṭaqs ṣaḥw al-yawm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weather is clear today.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صحو}} (\emph{ṣaḥw}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-ḥ-w}, \textquotedblleft{}to be cloudless\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives it of a day when the clouds have gone.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣaḥw}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣaḥw}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭ-ṭaqs ṣaḥw al-yawm.} — The weather is clear today.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for drought, then the Arabic for to evaporate, then say \emph{ṣaḥw} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{صحو} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Clear weather; cloudless\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{قوس} \ar{قزح} (qaws quzaḥ)}{قوس قزح (qaws quzaḥ)}]{\ar{قوس} \ar{قزح} (qaws quzaḥ) — a rainbow}

\label{lesson:AR-C485-qaws-quzah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to evaporate, then the Arabic for clear weather.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{قوس} \ar{قزح}}
\textbf{\ar{قوس} \ar{قزح}} — \emph{qaws quzaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a rainbow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ظهر} \ar{قوس} \ar{قزح} \ar{بعد} \ar{المطر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ẓahara qaws quzaḥ baʿda al-maṭar.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A rainbow appeared after the rain.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{قوس} \ar{قزح}} (\emph{qaws quzaḥ}) is \textquotedblleft{}the bow of \emph{quzaḥ}\textquotedblright{}: \emph{qaws}, \textquotedblleft{}a bow\textquotedblright{}, is built on the native root \emph{q-w-s} (Lane), but the origin of \emph{quzaḥ} is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qaws quzaḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ẓahara qaws quzaḥ baʿda al-maṭar.} — A rainbow appeared after the rain.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to evaporate, then the Arabic for clear weather, then say \emph{qaws quzaḥ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ندى} (nadā)}{ندى (nadā)}]{\ar{ندى} (nadā) — dew}

\label{lesson:AR-C485-nada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for clear weather, then the Arabic for a rainbow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ندى}}
\textbf{\ar{ندى}} — \emph{nadā} — \textquotedblleft{}dew\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{الندى} \ar{على} \ar{العشب} \ar{في} \ar{الصباح}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna an-nadā ʿalā al-ʿushb fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was dew on the grass in the morning.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ندى}} (\emph{nadā}) is usually traced to the native Arabic root \emph{n-d-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to be moist\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nadā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nadā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna an-nadā ʿalā al-ʿushb fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ.} — There was dew on the grass in the morning.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for clear weather, then the Arabic for a rainbow, then say \emph{nadā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{ندى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Dew\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أشرق} (ashraqa)}{أشرق (ashraqa)}]{\ar{أشرق} (ashraqa) — to shine; to rise (of the sun)}

\label{lesson:AR-C485-ashraqa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a rainbow, then the Arabic for dew.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أشرق}}
\textbf{\ar{أشرق}} — \emph{ashraqa} — \textquotedblleft{}to shine; to rise (of the sun)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أشرقت} \ar{الشمس} \ar{بعد} \ar{الضباب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ashraqat ash-shams baʿda aḍ-ḍabāb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The sun came out after the fog.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يشرق}, \emph{yushriq}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أشرق}} (\emph{ashraqa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-r-q}, \textquotedblleft{}to rise (of the sun)\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV; \emph{sharq}, \textquotedblleft{}east\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{shurūq}, \textquotedblleft{}sunrise\textquotedblright{}, share the root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ashraqa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ashraqa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ashraqat ash-shams baʿda aḍ-ḍabāb.} — The sun came out after the fog.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a rainbow, then the Arabic for dew, then say \emph{ashraqa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أشرق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To shine; to rise (of the sun)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أظلم} (aẓlama)}{أظلم (aẓlama)}]{\ar{أظلم} (aẓlama) — to grow dark}

\label{lesson:AR-C485-azlama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for dew, then the Arabic for to shine.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أظلم}}
\textbf{\ar{أظلم}} — \emph{aẓlama} — \textquotedblleft{}to grow dark\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أظلمت} \ar{السماء} \ar{قبل} \ar{العاصفة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aẓlamat as-samāʾ qabla al-ʿāṣifa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The sky grew dark before the storm.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يظلم}, \emph{yuẓlim}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أظلم}} (\emph{aẓlama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ẓ-l-m}, \textquotedblleft{}darkness\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV; \emph{ẓalām}, \textquotedblleft{}darkness\textquotedblright{}, shares the root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aẓlama}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aẓlamat as-samāʾ qabla al-ʿāṣifa.} — The sky grew dark before the storm.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for dew, then the Arabic for to shine, then say \emph{aẓlama} again
\end{itemize}
